source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF abstract explicitly links https://github.com/mrflogs/LoRA-Pre. Read-only gh repo view and gh api inspection of main found only LICENSE and README.md; the README title and repository description exactly match the paper and state that code/training scripts are still being prepared. Exact-title gh repository search returned this repository as the only paper-specific match; no plot*, figure*, visual*, table*, .ipynb, .tex, .tikz, .pgf, .svg, style, or data file was available for the PDF objects. The raster/vector assets visible in the PDF are therefore not recorded as public source files.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 2–3 use a four-color categorical Matplotlib-like palette (#1F77B4, #FF7F0E, #2CA02C, #D62728) for method/rank; Tables 1–3 use Royal Blue citation links and pale-cyan proposed-row shading; Figure 1 uses independent pastel semantic fills. Table weights/underlines and Figure 2's dashed Adam line provide limited redundant encoding.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 1 and all tables are PDF vector/text objects; Figure 2 contributes two embedded RGB raster XObjects and Figure 3 one embedded RGB raster XObject, each with a soft mask. Raster plots are inspected at 200 dpi page rendering and original extracted-image resolution.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern keeps the text and tables coherent. Figure 2–3 DejaVu Sans raster plots are broadly compatible but small; Figure 1's Comic Sans/pastel diagram is a conspicuous local style break. Color semantics are consistent within plot pairs and within tables but not unified across the whole paper.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Illustration of our LoRA-Pre method. In this work, we establish a novel connection: the exponential moving average (EMA) update for optimizer momentum is mathematically equivalent to training a linear regressor using online gradient descent. Leveraging this equivalence, we propose compressing the optimizer states (i.e., the momenta) using low-rank matrices to reduce the memory footprint. Finally, the closed-form update rules for these matrices without requiring back-propagation are given by Theorem 3.1.

color.semantic_mapping: Black carries equations and outlines; #FFFBF0 is the enclosure; blue arrows and m_A encode the compression/equivalent-form stages; peach m/m_B and gray gradient-history traces distinguish roles.

encodings.x: left-to-right computational stages: EMA/equivalent form → low-rank compression → factor updates
encodings.y: vertical correspondence between EMA and online gradient flow
encodings.color: pastel fills identify transformation and factor roles; gray marks incoming/history gradients
encodings.shape: direction arrows, central rectangle m, and paired m_B/m_A trapezoids
encodings.line: solid arrows/shape outlines plus dashed outer enclosure and gradient-history traces
encodings.text: equations and direct labels: Equivalent Form, Low-Rank Compression, Online Gradient Flow, and update

figures.data_and_statistics: No empirical data, aggregation, denominator, unit, or uncertainty. The marks are symbolic equations, matrix factors, and arrows expressing EMA/online-regression equivalence and the low-rank Newton update.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction problem of optimizer-state memory → Section 3.2 equations (7)–(9) establish EMA as online regression → Section 3.3 equation (10) and Theorem 3.1 equations (11)–(12) give the factor update → Figure 1 summarizes the method interface → Appendix A pp.13–14 supplies the proof.
design_strengths: A single left-to-right path joins objective, equivalent form, compression operation, and executable factor update.
Equations remain next to the structure they define, so the diagram is more than an abstract block schematic.
Position, shape, labels, and light fills provide partially redundant cues.
design_weaknesses: Comic Sans MS and pastel styling visibly depart from the Nimbus/Computer Modern paper style.
The second-derivative inverse expressions and several labels are dense at double-column reading size.
Matrix dimensions, gray history traces, and arrow semantics are not independently keyed; complete interpretation requires Section 3.3 and Appendix A.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place symbolic objective, equivalent rewrite, compression action, and closed-form update on one directed canvas, with each equation directly attached to its stage.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Rank efficiency comparison across efficient optimization methods. Perplexity versus rank for 60M (left) and 130M (right) models, demonstrating LoRA-Pre’s superior performance at lower ranks compared to baseline methods.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue=GaLore, orange=LoRA-Pre Adam, green=LoRA-Pre Muon, red=full Adam baseline; red also uses a dashed line.

encodings.color: method series using blue/orange/green/red categorical palette
encodings.line: solid method trajectories; red dashed horizontal full-Adam reference
encodings.facet: two panels by model size: (a) 60M and (b) 130M
encodings.text: panel titles, axis labels, ticks, repeated legends, and (a)/(b) labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Each panel has four rank settings for four series, all shown as single perplexity point estimates. There are no seeds, repeats, error bars, bands, intervals, or failure values. One horizontal Adam baseline is drawn per panel. Rank values are plotted at equal categorical spacing rather than proportional numeric spacing.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4.3 rank-ablation design → Figure 2 compares GaLore, LoRA-Pre Adam, LoRA-Pre Muon, and Adam across two model sizes → p.9 interprets rank=16 versus GaLore rank=128/256 as 8×/16× efficiency → the proposed explanation is continuous subspace adaptation.
design_strengths: The two model sizes share a metric and visual grammar, enabling immediate side-by-side rank comparisons.
A full-Adam dashed reference makes the low-rank/performance trade-off legible without another panel.
Fixed colors and discrete rank points make the rank-efficiency headline easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: Equal visual spacing hides the ratio difference between rank intervals.
Four low-perplexity curves crowd the lower edge, while the repeated legends consume plot area.
No uncertainty or run count is shown, so close curves cannot be judged against run-to-run variation.
The embedded raster and small double-column text reduce tick and legend legibility.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched model-size panels with a fixed method palette and a dashed full-method reference to turn a discrete resource-budget ablation into a direct visual comparison.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Test perplexity for LoRA-Pre Muon with different ranks during training.

color.semantic_mapping: Color identifies rank=16, 64, 128, and 256 respectively; all trajectories use the same marker and solid line.

encodings.text: in-plot title, axis labels, iteration ticks, and rank legend

figures.data_and_statistics: The 130M LoRA-Pre Muon run is shown at roughly twenty equally spaced checkpoints per rank. Values are single test-perplexity point estimates; no repeats, error bands, error bars, or interval definitions are provided.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2 endpoint/rank comparison → Figure 3 follows LoRA-Pre Muon rank trajectories during training → p.9 interprets the shrinking initial gap as evidence for dynamic subspace updates → supports a mechanism/robustness explanation rather than a statistical uncertainty claim.
design_strengths: A trajectory view adds convergence dynamics to Figure 2's endpoint comparisons.
Shared axes and a fixed rank palette make the initial gap and later convergence visible.
design_weaknesses: Single-column raster placement leaves little room for readable legend, title, and dense iteration ticks.
The caption omits the 130M model and explicit rank list, so it is not self-contained.
No uncertainty, seed count, or checkpoint definition is supplied; close late-stage curves cannot be interpreted quantitatively.
figures.reusable_pattern: After a discrete rank endpoint plot, add one common-axis trajectory plot showing the initial-gap-to-convergence pattern that the proposed mechanism predicts.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Comparison with low-rank algorithms on pre-training various sizes of Llama models on the C4 dataset. We report the validation perplexity (↓) on a hold-out C4 test set. The best and second-best performance within the low-rank optimizers are highlighted with bold and underline. ∗ denotes the results are reproduced by ourselves.

tables.uncertainty: None: one validation-perplexity point per model/optimizer; no seeds, repeats, dispersion, interval, or failure-rate column.
tables.data_and_statistics: Hold-out C4 validation perplexity (↓, lower is better) for 60M, 130M, 350M, and 1B Llama models. The header also reports r/d_model and training tokens. Rows cover full Adam/Muon, seven low-rank baselines, and LoRA-Pre Adam/Muon; Fira* marks reproduced values and Low-Rank at 1B is 142.53.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 4.1 memory-efficient pre-training design → Table 1 supplies the cross-scale main comparison → the text interprets LoRA-Pre Adam/Muon ranking and 0.81/2.45/1.6 perplexity gaps → Appendix B Algorithms 1–2 provide the optimizer instantiations. The table supports the performance headline, not a directly measured memory claim.
design_strengths: Model scale, rank/hidden-size metadata, training tokens, and results are on one horizontal decision surface.
Full optimizers, low-rank baselines, and proposed rows are separated by rules and retain conspicuous poor values.
Bold/underline explicitly encode best/second-best within the low-rank comparison.
design_weaknesses: The multi-row header does not state whether every baseline's rank is controlled identically beyond the listed metadata.
Single point estimates cannot establish whether close differences are stable.
Cyan full-row shading plus bold/underline makes the proposed rows visually heavy, while memory bytes, throughput, wall-clock, and failure rate are absent.
tables.reusable_pattern: Combine scale and budget metadata with complete baseline rows, direction arrows, and explicit best/second-best rules so a main performance claim can be checked without a separate legend.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Results of memory-efficient fine-tuning methods. We compare our method with efficient fine-tuning methods including LoRA (Hu et al., 2022), rsLoRA (Kalajdzievski, 2023), and DoRA (Liu et al., 2024), and an efficient optimizer GaLore (Zhao et al., 2024). The models are fine-tuned on the MetaMath100k (Yu et al., 2024) dataset, and evaluated on GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) and MATH-500 (Lightman et al., 2024). We highlight the best performance on Adam-like optimizer and Muon-like optimizer with bold.

tables.uncertainty: None: one score/average per model, task, and optimizer family; no seed dispersion, interval, or sample-size uncertainty is reported.
tables.data_and_statistics: GSM8K and MATH-500 scores plus their arithmetic Average for Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-2-7B. Five Adam-like rows and three Muon-like rows are separated; best values within each optimizer family are bold. The same-rank and training configuration are described in the surrounding Section 4.2 text rather than the table header.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 4.2 MetaMath100k fine-tuning design → Table 2 combines model, task, and optimizer-family comparisons → the text reports Average improvements of 2.59/4.88/1.96/6.03 → Appendix B supports Adam/Muon compatibility. Average is a headline summary and cannot replace task-level interpretation.
design_strengths: Two-level model→task headers keep six task cells and two averages aligned.
Adam-like and Muon-like row groups make optimizer-family comparisons explicit.
Task-level values remain visible alongside Average, and proposed rows are lightly shaded with bold best values.
design_weaknesses: Average is not labeled as an equal-weight arithmetic mean.
Rank, learning rate, and other training controls are not part of the table itself.
No uncertainty is shown; bold best values are family-relative and the Muon MATH-500 6.15 tie is not marked as a tie.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a model-group × task-subcolumn × optimizer-family row structure, retaining both task-level scores and a clearly defined summary metric.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Results of pre-training using different efficient Muon optimizers.

tables.uncertainty: None: one validation-perplexity point per model size and optimizer; no repeats, dispersion, interval, or implementation-cost uncertainty.
tables.data_and_statistics: 60M/130M/350M pre-training validation perplexity (lower is better). Full Muon is the reference upper-performance bound, Muon w/o momentum is the lower reference, GaLore Muon and Fira Muon are adapted projection baselines, and LoRA-Pre Muon is the proposed row.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 4.3 low-rank Muon-optimizer ablation → Table 3 tests projection-baseline transfer to Muon → the text interprets 3.54/1.80/0.43 gaps and projection methods falling below Muon without momentum → Algorithm 2 gives the proposed Muon implementation.
design_strengths: Full, no-momentum, adapted-baseline, and proposed rows form a legible upper/lower/efficient comparison.
Three model sizes are aligned in one row, and negative projection-baseline results are retained rather than omitted.
design_weaknesses: The caption omits dataset, metric direction, upper/lower reference roles, and the Muon adaptation context.
Second-best gaps and implementation differences cannot be checked from the caption alone.
Single point estimates do not establish stability of the counterintuitive baseline ordering.
tables.reusable_pattern: For optimizer transfer, place full, no-momentum, adapted baseline, and proposed variants in the same table so both success and transfer failure are visible.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Sensitivity Analysis of Momentum Parameters β. We report the validation perplexity on the 60M model. The method exhibits stability around the default settings derived from standard Adam (β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.95). Extreme values (e.g., β → 1) cause the implicit γ to vanish, leading to training instability.

tables.uncertainty: None: six single-run validation-perplexity points with a discrete Stable/Optimal/Diverged status; no variance, run count, or divergence criterion is defined.
tables.data_and_statistics: 60M LoRA-Pre Adam validation perplexity. With the other coefficient fixed, β₁ takes 0.90/0.95/0.99 and β₂ takes 0.90/0.95/0.999. Default values and Optimal are bold; Default is italic; extreme values are explicitly marked Diverged.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix D.1 derives (1−γ₁)^2=β₁ and (1−γ₂)^4=β₂ → Table 4 scans β₁/β₂ around the standard defaults → the appendix text links γ→0 to slow subspace adaptation and divergence. It is the only appendix table and connects the coupling mechanism to robustness/failure evidence.
design_strengths: Fixed-other-parameter row groups make the two one-dimensional sensitivity scans distinguishable.
Perplexity and Stable/Optimal/Diverged status share one decision surface, retaining failure rows.
Bold, italic, and status text encode defaults and failures without relying on color.
design_weaknesses: Six points cannot delimit the claimed reasonable range.
Status has no divergence threshold, training-step criterion, or reproducibility information.
The table is appendix-only and its restrictions are not recalled in the main headline tables.
tables.reusable_pattern: For analytically coupled hyperparameters, use fixed-condition short scans with numeric performance and explicit stable/failure states, retaining extreme failures.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the EMA→online-regression→low-rank interface; Table 1 gives cross-scale pre-training; Table 2 gives cross-model/task/optimizer fine-tuning; Figure 2 turns rank efficiency into a two-panel endpoint comparison; Figure 3 adds trajectory evidence; Table 3 tests Muon transfer; Table 4 moves β–γ sensitivity and failures to the appendix.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 1/2 and Table 2/4 use bold caption titles and explain setup; Table 1's unbolded caption is nevertheless detailed; Table 3 is only a short title; Figure 3 omits model size, rank list, and the main finding. Figures more often state a conclusion, while tables mostly describe settings and leave the numerical conclusion to prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses Model Size plus r/d_model and Training Tokens tiers; Table 2 uses model→task tiers; Tables 3–4 use one header tier. Group rules and Method separators support scanning, while cyan proposed rows and blue citation links are not exhaustively explained in every caption.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 maps equations (7)–(12) to the method interface; Tables 1–2 are pre-training/fine-tuning main comparisons; Figures 2–3 and Table 3 test rank, dynamic subspace, and Muon transfer; Table 4 tests the Appendix D coupling. Appendix A/B/C supply proof, algorithms, and convergence bounds but no new Figure/Table.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figure 1 points to Theorem 3.1, proved in Appendix A pp.13–14; the main text points to Algorithms 1–2 on pp.15/17; Appendix C pp.17–23 contains approximation/convergence analysis; Appendix D p.23 contains the only appendix table. The figures/tables do not expose the theory assumptions, initialization details, or run dispersion.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Text and table typography is consistently Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern at about 10 pt. Raster plot text is estimated DejaVu Sans and small. Figure 1 embeds Comic Sans MS for labels, creating the strongest typography discontinuity.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figures 2–3 share the blue/orange/green/red plot palette, while Tables 1–3 share Royal Blue links and cyan proposed-row fills. Figure 1 uses separate pastel colors. Within-object encoding is readable, but LoRA-Pre has no single cross-object accent and most plots are not grayscale-safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1's single path from symbolic objective through equivalence and compression to a closed-form update.
Table 1's combination of scale, rank/hidden-size, training tokens, complete baselines, and explicit best/second-best rules.
The Figure 2→Figure 3 pair: discrete rank endpoint comparison followed by a trajectory check of the proposed dynamic mechanism.
Table 3's full/no-momentum/adapted-baseline/proposed contrast and Table 4's retention of Stable/Diverged rows.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: method interface and theory intuition.
Table 2: cross-task and cross-optimizer decision surface.
failure_patterns: Every empirical object lacks seed count, repeats, and uncertainty.
Figure 2 treats non-equally spaced ranks as equally spaced categorical positions.
Figure 3 is small, raster, and caption-incomplete.
Table 3's caption is too short to stand alone.
Tables emphasize low-rank performance without measured memory/time, and Figure 1's Comic Sans/pastel treatment is inconsistent with the rest of the paper.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper establishes EMA-to-low-rank updates with one theory diagram, then makes the low-rank performance claim scannable through cross-scale tables and rank/optimizer ablations, while leaving uncertainty, measured cost, and several applicability conditions outside the visual objects.
